SESSIONS JUDGE BELAGAVI FOR

THE  OFFENCES P/U/SEC. 498A, 307 OF IPC AGAINST THE  PETITIONER/ACCUSED.
 -2-  CRL.P No. 100785 of 2023  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
Though the case is listed before the Court for admission, the complainant and the petitioner - accused are present before the Court.
2. On behalf of the complainant, Smt.Pallavi Palekar files power.
3. Both the counsel submitted a joint compromise petition.
Parties are identified by the respective counsels and the proof in the form of Aadhar card,
Photographs of parties are also produced.
4. The contents of the compromise petition are read over to the parties and they agree that there is no force, undue influence or coercion in reaching out the terms of the compromise.
In fact, the parties who are husband and wife are also now separated with a decree of divorce.
One of the conditions for the decree of divorce is to bring the pending criminal litigation to a logical end.
Accordingly, they have filed the present petition.

5. Since the compromise is voluntary and it is part of the decree of divorce, following the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ramgopal and another vs. state of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2021 SCC online SC 834., continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioner would end up in a futile exercise.

entities.text: Ramgopal and another vs. state of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2021 SCC online SC 834
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER
Placing the compromise petition on record, the criminal petition is allowed.
Pending criminal proceedings in S.C.No.57/2022 (C.C.No.158/2021) pending before the V Addl. Sessions Judge, Belagavi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 307 of IPC are hereby quashed.
